findings.gate_said: Primary analysis (NEJM 2016): HR 0.556, 95% CI 0.429–0.720. Updated analysis (Ann Oncol 2018): HR 0.568, 95% CI 0.457–0.704. NEJM OS paper (2022) rounds the updated PFS HR to 0.57, 95% CI 0.46–0.70. No source gives HR 0.56 with CI 0.45–0.70.
findings.why: CLOSED BY RE-TEST against the record, 2026-09-12: the operator answered this as S001-07 on 2026-08-29, two days BEFORE the 31 August gate run that raised it. ANSWER (Fred Ugast, 2026-08-29, verbatim): "The guideline lists MONALEESA-2 at HR 0.56 (0.45-0.70), MONARCH 3 at 0.54 (0.41-0.72), PALOMA-2 at 0.58 (0.46-0.72). The figure 0.57 does not appear in the guideline." The gate's WRONG_VALUE was not wrong about the publications -- NEJM 2016 prints 0.556 (0.429-0.720), Ann Oncol 2018 prints 0.568 (0.457-0.704), NEJM 2022 rounds to 0.57 (0.46-0.70) -- and was wrong about the guideline, which prints its own rounding, a third value. It could not have known: the licence forbids any automated reader opening S001, so the gate tested the page's claim about the guideline against everything except the guideline. The durable state that lets a check consult the operator's answer is findings.attestation_for, added the same day.

The spending function is Lan–DeMets; O'Brien–Fleming describes the boundary shape used within that function. The total two-sided type I error of 0.05 was split between ITT (0.04) and sVD (0.01) via a graphical approach, not simply 'divided
findings.quote: The cumulative type I error rate within each population was maintained using the Lan–DeMets spending function with O’Brien–Fleming boundary
findings.why: ACCEPTED 2026-09-13 (C95-001). Both page sentences called O’Brien–Fleming the spending function; the paper names Lan–DeMets as the spending function and O’Brien–Fleming as the boundary. The quote is what the RENDERED page 2 prints (pdftoppm, F1); the PDF's text layer renders it 'Lane DeMets spending function with O’BrieneFleming boundary', declared text_layer: defective on S003's record (F3), so the quotation check reports cannot-evaluate against this rendition rather than pass or fail. F2 (a sound rendition) was attempted and refused: Europe PMC inEPMC N; annalsofoncology.org and sciencedirect.com 403 to a script.

findings.gate_said: HR 0.804 (0.637–1.015) is confirmed as the correct final OS figure for MONARCH 3 itself (Annals of Oncology 2024; PMC full text of the Scientific Reports paper does not display the per-trial HR table in the snippets retrieved)
findings.why: CLOSED BY RE-TEST 2026-09-13 against the held bytes of S015 -- its Table 1, held since today as a second representation (Nature serves the table as its own page, so the article HTML held since 1 September never contained it). The table, verbatim: study row "Study characteristics CDK4/6i with AI or tamoxifen CDK4/6i with fulvestrant PAL-2 MONALEESA-2 MONALEESA-7 MONARCH-3 PALOMA-3 MOLANEESA-3 MONARCH 2"; "Reported HR for OS 0.956 0.76 0.76 0.804 0.814 0.73 0.757"; "Reported 95% CI for HR of OS 0.777–1.177 0.63–0.93 0.61–0.96 0.637–1.015"; "Year of updated data 2022 2022 2022 2023". MONARCH-3 is the fourth column by the study row, so its reported HR for OS is 0.804 with 95% CI 0.637–1.015 and its year of updated data is 2023 -- exactly what the page says. The gate's NOT_FOUND was a fact about what it could reach (it said so: 'the PMC full text ... does not display the per-trial HR table in the snippets retrieved'). Dates: S015 accepted 29 January 2024, published 7 February 2024; it cites MONARCH 3's final OS via SABCS abstract GS01-12 (December 2023); S003 published the same figure online 8 May 2024.

findings.gate_said: The draft later corrects itself by noting that PALOMA-2 was powered for overall survival and MONARCH 3 was not — but this sentence, which will be read and quoted on its own, implies all four trials were powered only for progression-free survival. That is false for PALOMA-2. The sentence contradicts the draft's own later correction.
findings.why: CLARIFIED 2026-09-13, not a correction. The sentence asserted nothing false; the clause 'every one of these trials was powered to measure' was restrictive, not exhaustive; naming the endpoint removes the ambiguity the gate read into it. Now reads: 'On progression-free survival, the endpoint all four trials were powered to measure, nothing separates them.' Bound to the four trials' primary-endpoint records (S005/S019, S003, S009/S020, S007/S022). No claim added about what PALOMA-2 was or was not additionally powered for.

Saying HARMONIA 'did not separate them' implies a null efficacy result, when the correct statement is that HARMONIA produced no efficacy result at all. The draft elsewhere correctly says HARMONIA 'establishes that the compar
findings.why: DISMISSED BY RE-TEST 2026-09-13. The attacked wording ('…and neither separated them') is no longer on the page. The sentence as published now reads, in full: "Two randomised trials have tested one of these drugs against another — both ribociclib against palbociclib, neither in the population the guideline sentence describes. One found no significant difference between them; the other stopped at 61 patients and never reported, so it establishes nothing either way. None has tested abemaciclib against either of the others, which is the pair the category difference turns on." It already says HARMONIA established nothing either way, which is what the gate's correct_reading asked for. The 12 September re-test recorded this finding as 'live' on a partial string match (the first 80 characters of the attacked sentence survived the revision); that outcome was wrong in kind, and the re-test now reports 'partly' for that case and requires a disposition naming the current sentence, which this is.
